stem:
A grouped frequency distribution with unequal class widths has the following data.

Class: 0-10, Frequency: 12
Class: 10-20, Frequency: 18
Class: 20-40, Frequency: 30
Class: 40-50, Frequency: 16
Class: 50-80, Frequency: 24

In a correctly drawn histogram (where bar height represents frequency density), which class has the tallest bar?

per_option_rationale.rationale: Choosing the class with the highest raw frequency (30 in 20-40) instead of highest frequency density. For unequal widths, raw frequency does not determine bar height.
Selecting class 50-80 because it has a relatively large frequency (24) without noting its wide class width (30) reduces its density to only 0.8.
Selecting class 0-10 because it is first or without computing densities; its density is 1.2, lower than 10-20's density of 1.8.

explanation: For unequal class widths, histogram bar height = frequency density = frequency / class width. Compute for each class: 0-10: 12/10=1.2, 10-20: 18/10=1.8, 20-40: 30/20=1.5, 40-50: 16/10=1.6, 50-80: 24/30=0.8. The maximum density is 1.8 for class 10-20, so class 10-20 has the tallest bar.

explanation_sections.punchline: Tallest bar = highest frequency density = 10-20 (density 1.8), not 20-40 which merely has the highest raw frequency.
explanation_sections.approach: Identify the model: histogram with unequal class widths requires frequency density. Recipe: (1) compute frequency density = frequency / class width for every class; (2) rank the densities; (3) identify the maximum. Densities: 0-10: 12/10=1.2; 10-20: 18/10=1.8; 20-40: 30/20=1.5; 40-50: 16/10=1.6; 50-80: 24/30=0.8. Maximum = 1.8 at class 10-20. The hidden trap: class 20-40 has the largest raw frequency (30) but its density (1.5) is second, not first.
explanation_sections.lesson: When class widths are unequal, histogram bar height is frequency density (f/h), not raw frequency. A wide class with high frequency can have a low bar; check every class.
explanation_sections.timing: 60-90 seconds. Compute all five densities: write each as fraction then compare. The critical insight is that the wide class 20-40 (width 20) and very wide class 50-80 (width 30) dilute their frequencies. Trap: most students pick 20-40 (highest raw frequency = 30) without dividing by class width.
